holidays.name: National Chocolate Covered Anything Day
holidays.description: A day to dip, drizzle, and drench absolutely everything in chocolate. Pretzels, bacon, potato chips, strawberries, and even more questionable items are all fair game.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday that popped up in food-calendar listings, likely inspired by the holiday season's peak in candy-making and the general human conviction that chocolate improves everything.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate-covered bacon has become a state fair staple, and chocolate-covered insects like crickets and ants are sold as gourmet snacks in some parts of the world.

holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Anything Day's Rival: Barbie and Barney Backlash Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek pop culture observance for people who want to gleefully retire their most annoying childhood earworm theme songs. Participants hum, then immediately regret it.
holidays.origin: This is an informal internet-born observance that circulates on social media, poking fun at kids' TV characters whose catchy songs get stuck in parents' heads for decades.
holidays.funFact: Scientists call a song that sticks in your head an 'earworm,' a term borrowed from the German word 'Ohrwurm.'

holidays.name: Underdog Day
holidays.description: A day to root for the little guy, whether that's a scrappy sports team, a long-shot candidate, or the cartoon superhero dog himself. Celebrate perseverance against the odds.
holidays.origin: Underdog Day is tied to the 1960s cartoon character Underdog, a humble shoeshine boy who secretly transformed into a heroic, rhyming canine crime fighter. The observance was created to celebrate perseverance and the spirit of the underdog.
holidays.funFact: Underdog first aired in 1964, and the character later became a giant balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, flying high above the crowds.

holidays.name: Day of Reconciliation (South Africa)
holidays.description: A public holiday in South Africa dedicated to fostering unity and reconciliation among the country's diverse communities after the end of apartheid.
holidays.origin: The date was previously observed as the Day of the Vow, commemorating the 1838 Battle of Blood River, and as Dingane's Day. After apartheid ended, it was reimagined in 1994 as a day of national unity.
holidays.funFact: The same date carries two very different historical meanings, and the holiday was deliberately repurposed to turn a symbol of division into one of togetherness.

holidays.name: Bahrain National Day
holidays.description: Bahrain celebrates its national day with fireworks, parades, flags, and lights draped across the island kingdom, turning the streets into a festive sea of red and white.
holidays.origin: The holiday marks the accession of Sheikh Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa as ruler in 1961, and it is also used to celebrate Bahrain's independence from Britain, which was actually declared in 1971.
holidays.funFact: Bahrain's name means 'two seas' in Arabic, a nod to the freshwater springs that bubble up from beneath the salty sea around the islands.
